body:
Path: `docs/adr/0046-package-docs-as-metadata.md` §3.2 (:138–:145) | Tier H — the maintainer's merge; the sanctioned form is the amended status line / supersession note, ⛔ not a rewrite of a dated record | graded by `domain:skills#2`

Filed by the `domain:cli` execution PM seat (#6024, session `session_01QCdUBjM47SxioST9z5Zwdf`) out of the #19359 round (PR #19406), where the delivering dev found it and declined to file — ⛔ correctly, because whether an ADR should be amended at all is a governance question, not a defect call. ⛔ Filed bare: `finding` only; `domain:*`, type and priority are triage's.

Dedupe words: `ADR-0046 3.2 last-write-wins` · `silently overwrite each other` · `ADR-0048 supersession not annotated` · `retired claim upstream source` · `org/type/name no package coordinate`.

## The source text, read verbatim from `origin/main`

`docs/adr/0046-package-docs-as-metadata.md`, lines 138–145:

> their uniqueness need is logical — the metadata registry key is `org/type/name` with **no package coordinate**, so two packages shipping the same bare name **silently overwrite each other (last-write-wins)**, and the console route `/docs/<name>` plus all cross-references key on the name.

⭐ That is the **whole inference** — premise *and* conclusion — and it is the ancestor of every downstream copy.

## ⚠️ It has already regenerated TWICE. This is measured, ⛔ not projected.

| downstream copy | card | state |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/cli/src/utils/collect-docs.ts` module header | **#19359** | fixed in PR #19406 |
| `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/pages.md` (Tier H, customer-published) | **#19358** | open |

⇒ fixing the two copies leaves the source able to regenerate it a **third** time. ⭐ That is the argument for this card existing at all: the downstream cards treat instances, this one treats the generator.

## What ADR-0048 actually did to it, and why the premise was never fully true

- **§1.2** is headed *"The silence is in the read, not the write"*.
- The write is **already composite-keyed**. Verified by this seat on `origin/main`, `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts:3452`:
  ```ts
  const storageKey = packageId ? withDisc(`${packageId}:${baseName}`) : bareKey;
  ```
  and the `Overwriting` log at `:3455` fires only on `collection.has(storageKey)` — **the same composite key, i.e. the same package.**
- **§3.4** then retired the cross-package throw outright.

⚠️ The premise is **true of one key and false of the other**, which is why it reads so convincingly: `refKey` (`packages/metadata-core/src/types.ts:84`) really does return `` `${ref.org}/${ref.type}/${ref.name}` `` with no package coordinate — but that is the **cache key**, ⛔ not the key an overwrite would happen on.

⇒ the real residual is a **context-free first-match READ**, ⛔ not an overwrite — a posture §3.3 accepts by design.

## ⚠️ No supersession annotation sits on that passage

Measured: ADR-0046 mentions ADR-0048 exactly **twice**, at lines **335** and **525** — ⛔ neither is near line 142, and neither annotates this passage. Its status line reads **`Status: Proposed (2026-06-12, revised …)`**.

⭐ By contrast `content/docs/ui/doc-pages.mdx:92` **does** carry the supersession — *"The earlier 'one global URL per doc' framing from ADR-0046 was superseded by ADR-0048's package-scoped resolution."* ⇒ the prose page records what the ADR itself does not.

## ⛔ The reason this was NOT filed by the dev, stated rather than hidden

ADRs are **dated records**. Prime Directive #13's *"new ADR or amended status line"* is arguably satisfied by ADR-0048 simply existing, and `docs/adr/**` is **Tier H**.

⇒ ⭐ **this card does not assert that the ADR must be edited.** It asserts that the source of a claim retired twice over is unannotated, and that the cost of leaving it so is now measured at two cards. Whether the remedy is an amended status line, a pointer at §3.2, or deliberately nothing at all, is the reader's call.

## First act

Decide whether a superseded passage inside a dated record is amended at all. ⛔ Do not start by editing §3.2 — if the answer is "ADRs are immutable", the correct outcome is a recorded decision and this card closes, which is a complete result.
